name: Mysore Rasam
steps: Rinse toor dal and simmer with turmeric and 450 ml water for 30–40 minutes until completely soft, then mash. Soak tamarind in 150 ml warm water and strain out seeds and fibre.

Heat 5 g of the ghee and roast chana dal, coriander seeds, cumin, pepper and dried chilli over low heat until fragrant. Add coconut and stir until lightly golden, then cool and grind with 100 ml water.
Simmer chopped tomatoes, tamarind extract and salt with the remaining 500 ml water for 8 minutes. Add mashed dal and roasted paste and simmer gently for 5 minutes until aromatic.
Heat the remaining ghee, pop mustard and add curry leaves carefully. Pour into the rasam and finish with coriander; it should be a pourable broth, slightly richer than plain rasam.
notes: Base recipe for 4 adults. Cooking times are estimates; follow the texture and doneness cues. Jain suitability follows your saved ingredient choices.
